content_preview.title: Alibaba's Qwen4-Max Cuts Reported Task Costs but Trails Rivals on Independent and Agentic Benchmarks
content_preview.summary: Alibaba says Qwen4-Max cuts costs by around 60% over its predecessor. Artificial Analysis places it 43 on its Intelligence Index, below Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol and Kimi K3.1 Pro.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Background

Alibaba introduced Qwen4-Max on November 16, 2026, describing it in a [company blog post](https://www.alibabacloud.com/blog/alibaba-unveils-qwen4-max-new-ai-teammate-for-work-creativity-and-discovery_603783) as a new flagship with "2.4 trillion total parameters, native vision capabilities, and a one-million-token context window." The post says Qwen4-Max "activates only 71 billion per token—25% fewer activated parameters compared to Qwen3.8-Max at the same 2.4T scale." A follow-up ...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured Analysis piece (Background / Current situation / Implications) that examines how vendor-reported benchmarks and an independent aggregate index diverge for Qwen4-Max, rather than merely recapping the launch. Facts are cleanly separated from interpretation: the Implications section is explicitly flagged ('The following points restate what the sources say; they are not predictions') and draws only conclusions directly supported by the cited figures. Word count 1272, within the 800-2000 Analysis range.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 5 source snapshots read in full from disk (gunzip'd .html.gz; sha256 of decompressed content matches manifest.json for all 5: source-0 cd3db3c5..., source-1 1143bd66..., source-2 7f39c36e..., source-3 f74aa956..., source-4 80f80bb8...). No suspicious_patterns flagged in manifest.json for any source; none found on inspection. (1) alibabacloud.com/blog...603783 (Alibaba's Qwen4-Max launch post, Nov 16 2026): confirms 2.4T total params, native vision, 1M context, 71B active/token, '25% fewer activated parameters compared to Qwen3.8-Max at the same 2.4T scale', Work360 '~60%' cost reduction and '35% fewer tokens at High', $0.075/M cached input, '6th on Code Arena' - all article quotes verbatim. (2) alibabacloud.com/blog...603786 (enterprise post, Johnny Mai, Nov 17 2026): confirms same param counts/context window and the verbatim disclaimer quoted in the article ('compare Qwen4-Max with Qwen3.8-Max. They are not comparisons with any other provider's models.'). Reports a separate 58% cost figure not used by the article - no conflict since the article never cites that number. (3) VentureBeat (Carl Franzen): confirms the six-benchmark table numbers exactly (DeepSWE 75.7/69.3/74.2/75.2/75.5; Terminal-Bench 4.0 48.5/38.9/59.6/56.1/67.2; ProgramBench 31.5/28.0/65.0/52.5/25.0; APEX-Agents v1.1 72.1/63.3/73.5/60.0/65.5; AutomationBench-AA 72.5/56.2/69.5/64.9/73.3), the Intelligence Index chart (43/34/46/55/55/59/60/65), and the critical disclosure quote ('These figures reproduce Qwen's chart... They are not independently rerun results...') verbatim. FOUND TWO NON-VERBATIM QUOTES (see concerns). (4) The Decoder (Jonathan Kemper): confirms 'ranks second behind Kimi K3.1 Pro' is the outlet's own 'among Chinese models' framing (subheading literally reads 'Qwen4-Max ranks second among Chinese models'), the $3.27/$10.02/$3.68 Intelligence-Index-task costs, and the Agents' Last Exam / Humanity's Last Exam / HealthBench Professional quote, all verbatim. (5) artificialanalysis.ai model page: confirms Intelligence Index score 43, 'below average among other models in a similar price tier' (verbatim FAQ match), $1.50/$4.50 per-M pricing, and the $0.80/M blended rate at the site's stated 7:2:1 cache-hit/input/output ratio. Independent-source count: 3 of 5 (VentureBeat, The Decoder, Artificial Analysis) are independent of Alibaba; the other 2 are Alibaba's own Alibaba Cloud blog posts - meets the Analysis minimum of >=4 sources with >=2 independent. Allowlist: alibabacloud.com was not yet on config/source_allowlist.txt; independently confirmed as Alibaba Cloud's own official blog (bylined 'Alibaba Cloud Community' and Alibaba Cloud staff writer Johnny Mai, referencing Alibaba's own Qwen/QwenCloud/QwenWork products, '(c) 2026 Qwen' footer) and added with a justification comment in this same review commit. Anthropic disclosure: not required - Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.2 appear only as incidental names in competitor benchmark-comparison lists (policy's explicit carve-out); Anthropic is not the subject and not named in the headline/summary/lead, and no passage carries an Anthropic/'assisted by Claude' credit line.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All benchmark numbers, derived figures and comparisons recomputed against raw source text and confirmed correct: Qwen4-Max beats Qwen3.8-Max on 'every listed benchmark' in VentureBeat's six-benchmark table (verified all six pairs); Kimi K3.1 Pro's 46 is correctly 'three ahead of' Qwen4-Max's 43; VentureBeat's chart shows GPT-6.1 Sol/Sonnet 5.5/Opus 5.5/Gemini 4 Carbon/Fable 5.2 'all scoring higher' than 43 (55/55/59/60/65, all correct); $3.27 is correctly 'lower than both' $10.02 and $3.68. The headline and summary correctly preserve the vendor-vs-independent distinction ('Cuts Reported Task Costs' / 'Alibaba says ... Artificial Analysis places') per claim-accuracy Rule 13 and the editorial policy's Analysis requirements - vendor-reported cost/benchmark figures (Work360, Code Arena, the six-benchmark chart) are kept textually distinct from Artificial Analysis's independently-run Intelligence Index figures throughout. The VentureBeat benchmark table is explicitly and correctly labeled as reproducing Alibaba's own chart, not independently rerun ('These figures reproduce Qwen's chart... They are not independently rerun results'), satisfying the specific check requested for this review. The Decoder's 'second' ranking claim is correctly disambiguated by the article as a Chinese-models-only ranking rather than an overall one, which the outlet's own subheading supports - a disagreement between how two sources frame the same Intelligence Index number, explained rather than left unresolved, per claim-accuracy Rule 5. One recoverable issue found: two quotations attributed to VentureBeat paraphrase rather than reproduce the source verbatim (see concerns) - the underlying figures are accurate, only the quote-marked wording differs.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout. The single 'clearly' flagged by the automated loaded-language scanner ('a model that is cheaper and competitive on some tasks, and clearly behind on others') is a false positive: it appears in the policy-compliant Implications section as a sourced characterization of benchmarks already itemized in the body (Terminal-Bench 4.0, ProgramBench, Humanity's Last Exam, the aggregate Intelligence Index), not sensationalized language. No AI self-reference; no promotional framing of either Alibaba or its competitors.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Herald coverage of Qwen4-Max or this launch exists (checked src/content/articles/2026-11/ and grepped the full articles tree for 'qwen4'/'qwen4-max'/'qwen 4' - no hits). The piece explicitly cross-references the Herald's existing Nov 13 Gemini 4 Hydrogen/Argon Artificial Analysis article as background on a recurring pattern this month; that internal link (/article/2026-11/13-artificial-analysis-scores-googles-gemini-4-hydrogen-51-against-argons-50-at-high-thinking-with-187-per-index-task-versus-497) resolves to an existing published file. New topic, not a duplicate.
concerns: Two quotations attributed to VentureBeat paraphrase rather than reproduce the source verbatim. Article: Alibaba 'reports cutting average task costs on Work360 "from $4.43 to $1.67, representing approximately 62% savings," with token consumption dropping "roughly 24% at the Xhigh reasoning setting and 35% at High."' VentureBeat's actual text: 'reducing the average cost of a task in its internal Work360 evaluation from $4.43 to $1.67, approximately 62%' (no 'representing'/'savings') and 'token consumption falls approximately 24% at the Xhigh reasoning setting and 35% at High on Work360' ('approximately', not 'roughly'). The underlying figures (4.43, 1.67, 62%, 24%, 35%) are all correct and accurately sourced to VentureBeat/Alibaba - only the quote-marked wording was lightly reworded rather than copied verbatim. Filed as a corrections record (clarification) rather than REJECT because it is a single, narrowly-scoped wording issue in the body, not the headline/summary/lead, and does not change any fact.
recommendations: Future submissions: when wrapping a paraphrase in quotation marks, either copy the source sentence exactly or drop the quote marks and attribute in reported speech.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Strong Analysis submission: meets the 800-2000 word range (1272 words), cites 5 sources with 3 independent of the subject (VentureBeat, The Decoder, Artificial Analysis) against 2 Alibaba-owned blog posts, examines a cross-vendor pattern (vendor benchmark charts vs. independent aggregate indices) rather than recapping a single release, and keeps facts and analysis in clearly separated sections. All benchmark and cost figures were verified against raw source text and recomputed where derived; the article correctly labels Alibaba's six-benchmark comparison chart as VentureBeat-reproduced rather than independently rerun, and keeps vendor-reported Work360/Code Arena figures textually separate from Artificial Analysis's own Intelligence Index measurements throughout, including in the headline and summary. The lone defect found is two non-verbatim quotations of accurate figures from VentureBeat, addressed via corrections record rather than rejection. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, well-sourced analysis of a frontier-model launch for an audience that already tracks LLM benchmarking, but not an industry-changing event.
